newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends Tokyo up on cash rate decline.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends Tokyo up on cash rate decline.

text.p: The key December three-month Euroyen futures contract ended the day session higher on Monday in response to falls in cash Euroyen rates, traders said.
Cash Euroyen rates fell as investors began to park funds in them, changing their previous stance of holding back investment until those cash rates climbed further.
The change in investment strategy reflected their view that the Bank of Japan (BOJ) may hold down rates for a while.
The key three-month cash Euroyen rate was traded at 0.58-0.57 percent, down from 0.59-0.58 percent on Friday.
The six-month cash Euroyen rate was traded at 0.67 percent, down from Friday's 0.675 percent.

"Some had expected the BOJ would let the key call rate rise above 0.5 percent as early as this month or June, but now many believe the central bank will delay such a move until July," said a trader at a European bank. He said the change in expectation was mostly due to the steep rise in the yen, which would keep inflation under control and hurt the earnings of exporters, which have been spearheading the economic recovery.
In the yen interest rate swap (IRS) market, some city banks received fixed interest rates for the short- to medium-term maturity, traders said.
These city banks were believed to have sold JGB futures contracts to hedge against their IRS positions.
The two-year IRS was quoted at 1.21/1.25 percent, down from 1.25/1.29 percent on Friday.
The BOJ, in its regular market operation at 0020 GMT, absorbed most of the market surplus via draining 500 billion yen from the money market.
